target.title: feat: publish integrations and Crabbox Agent Skill discovery
target.body:
## Summary

- publish the generic Crabbox Agent Skill at `skills/crabbox/SKILL.md`, keep the repo-discoverable `.agents/skills/crabbox/SKILL.md` byte-identical, and reject drift in the docs gate
- make Skill metadata activate when `crabbox.yaml`, `.crabbox.yaml`, or the `crabbox` CLI is detected, while retaining remote-compute and evidence triggers
- make `crabbox init --skill` repeatable for repositories that need shared and host-native discovery paths; validate local `crabbox/SKILL.md` destinations and preflight every target before writing
- publish digest-verified domain discovery from crabbox.sh using the Agent Skills discovery draft plus a cross-vendor AI Catalog / ARD manifest, HTML discovery link, and `Agentmap`
- document audited discovery behavior across agent clients and ecosystem installers instead of adding duplicate per-vendor Skill implementations or an MCP/plugin loader
- correct the Zed package to recognize `crabbox.yaml` and `.crabbox.yaml` (not unsupported `.crabbox.yml`), and document exact Zed and Herdr publication status

## Why

The generated Skill originally omitted required `name` and `description` frontmatter. The checked-in Skill also lived only under hidden `.agents`, which many clients discover directly but GitHub CLI excludes from normal Skill source discovery. Other clients use native roots such as `.claude/skills`, `.kiro/skills`, or `.cline/skills`.

This change establishes one generic implementation with several transport layers:

1. automatic in-repository discovery through `.agents/skills`
2. installer discovery through the non-hidden `skills/*/SKILL.md` convention
3. host-native copies generated explicitly with repeatable `--skill`
4. domain discovery through crabbox.sh
5. task-time discovery through an AI Catalog

The Skill remains a thin, reviewable instruction layer over the installed CLI. It does not load executable plugins, forward model credentials, bypass host approval, or add an MCP server.

## Ecosystem coverage

| Route | Coverage |
| --- | --- |
| `.agents/skills` | Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot / VS Code, Windsurf, Devin, Zed Agent, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, OpenCode, Roo, Amp, Warp, OpenHands, Letta, Mistral Vibe, and Goose via Summon |
| Native project roots | Claude Code, Junie, Kiro, Qwen Code, Factory Droid, and Cline through repeatable `crabbox init --skill` |
| GitHub CLI | `gh skill install openclaw/crabbox skills/crabbox --pin refs/heads/main --agent codex --scope project` |
| Skills CLI | `npx skills add https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox --skill crabbox` |
| Agent Skills domain discovery | `https://crabbox.sh/.well-known/agent-skills/index.json` with a SHA-256 digest over the published bytes |
| Cross-vendor resource discovery | `https://crabbox.sh/.well-known/ai-catalog.json` using AI Catalog `specVersion: 1.0` and draft ARD discovery signals |

The client matrix links each host's current primary documentation and explicitly warns that the Agent Skills format does not mandate one search path. Vendor plugin manifests remain a follow-up for host marketplaces; they do not improve automatic repository discovery over the shared Skill and standard installers.

## Publication follow-ups

- Herdr direct installation works; topic-driven marketplace indexing is tracked in https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/issues/1156.
- The Zed package is development-installable; the registry PR must pin a commit reachable from upstream after this merges and is tracked in https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/issues/1157.
- GitHub CLI resolves the current v0.39.0 release before the default branch, so documentation selects `refs/heads/main` until v0.39.1 contains the generic source.
- The Agent Skills domain protocol and ARD are drafts. GitHub Pages serves conventional JSON/Markdown MIME types; strict AI Catalog media-type consumers may require a future header-capable edge.

## Validation

No new local test suite was run for the follow-up commit, per contributor request.

Static/source checks completed:

- `gofmt` on the changed Go files
- `git diff --check`
- byte comparison of the canonical Skill and its `.agents` projection
- independent source-only audits of CLI behavior, Windows path handling, docs fixtures, current client paths, GitHub CLI resolution, Agent Skills discovery v0.2.0, and AI Catalog / ARD schemas

Inspectible discovery proof gathered from the repository checkout:

```text
Agent Skills validator: Skill is valid!
Codex CLI 0.144.5: crabbox -> .agents/skills/crabbox/SKILL.md
Gemini CLI 0.37.1: crabbox [Enabled] -> .agents/skills/crabbox/SKILL.md
OpenCode 1.15.10: crabbox -> .agents/skills/crabbox/SKILL.md
```

Before the follow-up commit, the initial PR head also passed `go test ./internal/cli -count=1`, `scripts/check-docs.sh`, and all 17 hosted checks. Fresh hosted checks on the new head: 15/15 passed.

## Security

- detection is instructional and does not grant permission to start paid infrastructure
- the Skill tells agents to inspect repo config and run `crabbox doctor`
- credentials and lifecycle remain owned by Crabbox and the invoking host
- domain catalogs advertise the same reviewed Markdown artifact; they do not install or execute it

Reproducibility: yes. from source: a `charset=utf-16le` response whose raw bytes encode U+FFFD will decode successfully through the charset-aware path but fail the new hard-coded fatal UTF-8 validation; a Response-like object can also reject `arrayBuffer()` while resolving `text()`.

target.title: fix(agents): use raw-byte fatal UTF-8 validation for response text fallback
target.body:
## Summary
Replace the post-decode U+FFFD sentinel check with raw-byte fatal UTF-8 validation in `readResponseText`'s `arrayBuffer` fallback path. Malformed bytes are rejected by `TextDecoder("utf-8", { fatal: true })` while legitimate U+FFFD characters (encoded as `0xEF 0xBF 0xBD`) are correctly preserved.

## What Problem This Solves
The previous approach checked `text.includes("�")` after `res.text()` to detect malformed UTF-8. This is incorrect because a server can intentionally send the literal U+FFFD character (`�`) as valid content — the sentinel check would silently discard it. The WHATWG `Response.text()` produces U+FFFD for BOTH cases:
- Malformed byte `0xFF` → silently replaced with `�`
- Valid UTF-8 sequence `0xEF 0xBF 0xBD` → correctly decoded as `�`

Without raw-byte access, these two cases are indistinguishable from the decoded string alone.

**Code evidence**: [web-shared.ts:300-326](src/agents/tools/web-shared.ts#L300-L326)

## Root Cause
- `Response.text()` uses the WHATWG forgiving UTF-8 decoder — there is no way to opt into fatal mode
- The post-decode U+FFFD check cannot distinguish legitimate U+FFFD from replacement characters
- The `arrayBuffer()` method is available on standard `Response` objects and provides raw bytes

## Why This Fix
When `arrayBuffer()` is available (standard Response), read raw bytes and validate with a two-phase approach:
1. `decodeResponseBytes()` — charset-aware decoder (handles declared charsets)
2. If the result contains `�`, cross-validate: run `new TextDecoder("utf-8", { fatal: true })` on the same raw bytes. If it throws → bytes were truly malformed → return empty. If it succeeds → the `�` is a legitimate character → return the decoded text.

When `arrayBuffer()` is not available (mock Response), fall back to `res.text()` without the guard — we cannot distinguish in this case.

## User Impact
- **Before (v1)**: Server sends `0xEF 0xBF 0xBD` (legitimate U+FFFD) → `readResponseText` returns `{ text: "" }` — **compatibility regression**
- **After (v2)**: Server sends `0xEF 0xBF 0xBD` → `readResponseText` returns `{ text: "Hi�!" }` — **preserved**
- **After (v2)**: Server sends `0xFF` (malformed) → `readResponseText` returns `{ text: "" }` — **rejected**

## Evidence
- **Legitimate U+FFFD**: strict decode passes → character preserved → **PASS**
- **Malformed bytes**: strict decode throws TypeError → returned empty → **PASS**
- Both cases covered by regression tests

## Real Behavior Proof

```bash
$ node --import tsx scripts/proof-web-shared-ufffd.mjs
=== Test 1: valid UTF-8 ===
Result: {"text":"Hello, world!","truncated":false,"bytesRead":13}
PASS

=== Test 2: malformed UTF-8 bytes (0xFF) ===
Result: {"text":"","truncated":false,"bytesRead":0}
PASS: malformed bytes rejected, returned empty

=== Test 3: legitimate U+FFFD (0xEF 0xBF 0xBD) ===
Result: {"text":"Hi�!","truncated":false,"bytesRead":6}
PASS: legitimate U+FFFD preserved

=== Test 4: text() fallback ===
Result: {"text":"fallback text","truncated":false,"bytesRead":13}
PASS

ALL PASS
```

## Tests and Validation
- `npx vitest run src/agents/tools/web-shared.test.ts` — 42 passed
- New tests: `returns empty when arrayBuffer provides malformed UTF-8 bytes`, `preserves legitimate U+FFFD when server intentionally sends it`, `returns empty when text() fallback rejects`

target.title: fix(ssh-verify): preserve active cooldown entries during prune
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The cooldown prune function evicts the oldest entry regardless of whether it has expired. During a burst of SSH probe failures, active (unexpired) cooldowns can be evicted, allowing re-probing before the intended cooldown period.

## Why This Change Was Made

The while-loop should only evict expired entries. Adding an expiry check prevents premature eviction of active cooldowns when the cache is full but no entries have expired yet.

## User Impact

Under sustained SSH probe failures, the cooldown mechanism may allow premature re-probing of recently-failed nodes.

## Evidence

All 57 tests pass across gateway-core, gateway-server, and gateway-client test suites.

target.title: fix(qqbot): bound remote media downloads with header and idle timeouts
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

QQBot remote-media downloads could hang indefinitely when an upstream CDN
accepted the connection, returned headers (and optionally one body chunk), then
stopped sending data. Two channel-owned callers were missing a body-idle bound:

- `getPlatformAdapter().downloadFile` called `readRemoteMediaBuffer` with no
  header/idle timeouts
- `file-utils.downloadFile` / `fetchMedia` had a 120s response-header timeout
  but did not forward `readIdleTimeoutMs`

## Why This Change Was Made

Propagate one consistent QQBot media timeout policy through the channel-owned
boundary, using the existing guarded remote-media reader contract:

- `responseHeaderTimeoutMs: 120_000`
- `readIdleTimeoutMs: 30_000`

`downloadFile` hard-codes that policy; `fetchMedia` forwards optional
`readIdleTimeoutMs` from `FetchMediaOptions`. No new downloader or config key.

## User Impact

**Before:** A stalled QQ media body could leave inbound/outbound media handling
waiting forever and retain Gateway resources.

**After:** Stalled bodies fail closed after 30s without data
(`Media download stalled: no data received for 30000ms`), releasing the
connection. Completing transfers are unchanged. Unusually slow-but-progressing
transfers remain allowed (idle timer resets on each chunk).

## Evidence

- Changed: `extensions/qqbot/src/bridge/bootstrap.ts`,
  `extensions/qqbot/src/bridge/bootstrap.test.ts`,
  `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/adapter/types.ts`,
  `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/utils/file-utils.ts`,
  `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/utils/file-utils.test.ts`
- Production paths:
  - `getPlatformAdapter().downloadFile` → `readRemoteMediaBuffer({ responseHeaderTimeoutMs: 120000, readIdleTimeoutMs: 30000 })`
  - `file-utils.downloadFile` → `fetchMedia({ …, readIdleTimeoutMs: 30000 })`
  - `fetchMedia` forwards `readIdleTimeoutMs` into the shared reader

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

Stalled QQBot remote-media bodies fail closed on the channel's 30s idle budget
instead of hanging. Completing downloads still succeed and still carry the same
120s/30s policy.

### Canonical reachability path

`getPlatformAdapter().downloadFile` / `file-utils.downloadFile` →
`fetchMedia` / direct `readRemoteMediaBuffer` → shared guarded reader
(`chunkTimeoutMs` / idle watchdog from `readIdleTimeoutMs`)

### Shared helper / provider constraint check

Uses existing `readRemoteMediaBuffer` header + idle options (same contract as
core media store). No second downloader; SSRF allowlist / redirect behavior
unchanged.

### Real environment tested

Live `node:http` media server on `127.0.0.1` (headers + one PNG chunk, then
stall; plus a completing `/small` body). Production QQBot callers are exercised
with the real `readRemoteMediaBuffer` reader; fetch is redirected to the local
socket so the proof stays on-machine while preserving caller-supplied
timeouts. Node v22.23.1, PR head `9d7687e69f39`.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  extensions/qqbot/src/bridge/media-idle-timeout.proof.test.ts \
  --reporter=verbose

# Focused argument-propagation regressions
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  extensions/qqbot/src/bridge/bootstrap.test.ts \
  extensions/qqbot/src/engine/utils/file-utils.test.ts \
  --reporter=verbose
```

### Evidence after fix

**Case A — `getPlatformAdapter().fetchMedia` stalled live body (idle=400ms)**

```text
Case A fetchMedia: {
  elapsedMs: 2632,
  idleMs: 400,
  recorded: {
    url: 'https://media.qq.com/assets/stall.png',
    responseHeaderTimeoutMs: 120000,
    readIdleTimeoutMs: 400
  },
  error: 'Failed to fetch media … Media download stalled: no data received for 400ms'
}
✓ fetchMedia forwards readIdleTimeoutMs and fails closed on a stalled live body
```

**Case B — `getPlatformAdapter().downloadFile` production 30s idle**

```text
Case B downloadFile: {
  elapsedMs: 30019,
  recorded: {
    url: 'https://media.qq.com/assets/stall.png',
    responseHeaderTimeoutMs: 120000,
    readIdleTimeoutMs: 30000
  },
  error: 'Failed to fetch media … Media download stalled: no data received for 30000ms'
}
✓ downloadFile applies production 120s/30s policy and fails closed on a stalled live body 30028ms
```

**Case C — `file-utils.downloadFile` completing control**

```text
Case C file-utils.downloadFile: {
  bytes: 7,
  recorded: {
    url: 'https://media.qq.com/assets/small.png',
    responseHeaderTimeoutMs: 120000,
    readIdleTimeoutMs: 30000
  }
}
✓ file-utils.downloadFile completes a live body and forwards the same timeout policy
```

```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  3 passed (3)
```

### Observed result after fix

1. Changed QQBot `downloadFile` passes `responseHeaderTimeoutMs=120000` /
   `readIdleTimeoutMs=30000` into the shared reader and rejects a live stalled
   body in ~30019ms with the idle error (not hung).
2. `fetchMedia` forwards a caller idle budget and fails closed on the same stall
   socket.
3. Completing `file-utils.downloadFile` still returns the full body and still
   forwards the production 120s/30s policy.

### What was not tested

- Live stall against real QQ CDN hosts (`*.qpic.cn` / `*.qq.com`) on the public
  internet (proof uses a local stall socket through the QQBot callers)
- Header-stall-only path (no body) for these callers

### Fix classification

bugfix — timeout/hang

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted. Author reviewed the QQBot-owned timeout propagation, replaced the
incorrect OpenAI video-gen proof previously pasted into this PR body, and
captured live QQBot-path stall/complete evidence.

target.title: fix(doctor): guard snapshot store load against corrupt JSON
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`loadSessionStoreForSnapshotScan` has no try/catch around JSON.parse. A corrupt snapshot store file causes an uncaught SyntaxError crash instead of returning an empty state.

## Why This Change Was Made

The function is exported at module scope. While the primary caller wraps it, any future direct caller would get an unhandled exception from corrupt JSON. This defensive guard makes the function self-protecting.

## User Impact

Prevents crash when loading a corrupt session snapshot store.

## Evidence

All 24 existing tests pass:

```
 ✓ |commands| doctor-session-snapshots.test.ts (24 tests) 187ms
   ✓ flags cached bundled skill locations from inactive and temp-backed runtime roots
   ✓ maps stale snapshot paths to structured findings and dry-run effects
   ✓ expands home-relative cached bundled skill locations before classifying them
   ✓ repairs stale imsg bundled paths to the generated plugin skill path
   ✓ repairs retired imsg paths even when cached under the current package skills root
   ✓ resolves the retired package skills root for moved-skill snapshot repairs
   ✓ ignores current bundled locations and unrelated workspace skill locations
   ✓ handles Windows current and stale bundled skill paths without false positives
   ✓ reports stale cached metadata while distinguishing the live runtime root
   ✓ scans resolvedSkills before session store normalization strips them
   ✓ hydrates blobbed skills prompts before scanning raw session stores
   ✓ reports stale cached metadata from configured session stores
   ✓ reports stale cached metadata from templated configured session stores
   ✓ repairs stale inline prompt paths
   ✓ preserves a supervised session added while the repair backup is pending
   ✓ rejects repair when the current store contains an invalid reserved session
   ✓ repairs stale promptRef blob paths
   ✓ drops stale legacy resolvedSkills cache entries
   ✓ drops resolvedSkills cache entries with stale sourceInfo paths
   ✓ preserves sessions with missing promptRef blobs
   ✓ handles missing blob gracefully without crashing or reporting false findings
   ✓ scoped replacement preserves unrelated content
   ✓ creates backup before repair
   ✓ is idempotent — second repair finds nothing
```

## Risk checklist

target.body:

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Feishu users in a direct message (DM) would receive a spurious "⚠️ This reply completed without visible content..." fallback message immediately after the assistant intentionally went silent (emitted only the `NO_REPLY` token). This is confusing and noisy: the assistant correctly decided not to reply, but the user still gets an unwanted message anyway.

## Why This Change Was Made

Feishu's default `blockReplyBreak: "message_end"` setting routes the final assistant text through `sendBlockReply` (dispatch `kind: "block"`), not `sendFinalReply` (`kind: "final"`). When the model's only visible output is `NO_REPLY`, the shared `normalizeReplyPayload` helper correctly detects this as an intentional silent skip and calls `onSkip(payload, { kind: "block", reason: "silent" })`. However, the Feishu dispatcher's `onSkip` handler only ever recorded the skip when `info.kind === "final"`, so `skippedFinalReason` stayed `null` for block-kind silent skips. `ensureNoVisibleReplyFallback` then treated the turn as an ordinary empty response and sent the "no visible content" fallback — a path that is reachable specifically in DMs, where silent finals are disallowed by policy (`src/shared/silent-reply-policy.ts`), and is on for `main`.

The fix widens the `onSkip` condition to also capture block-kind skips whose reason is `"silent"`, matching the intentional-silence signal already produced upstream. It intentionally stays narrow: non-silent block skips (e.g. `reason: "empty"`) still fall through and trigger the fallback exactly as before, so this does not weaken the existing "let the user know nothing came back" safety net for genuinely empty turns.

## User Impact

Feishu DM users who trigger an intentional silent (`NO_REPLY`) response no longer receive a confusing, unwanted "no visible content" fallback message. Behavior for genuinely empty (non-silent) responses is unchanged — those still get the fallback as before.

This PR is AI-assisted (built with Cursor/Claude); I reviewed and understand the change.

### Real dispatch-pipeline proof (added in response to ClawSweeper review)

The strongest evidence in this PR is two tests that drive the **actual production call path** — `createReplyDispatcherWithTyping` → shared `normalizeReplyPayload` → Feishu's real `onSkip` closure — instead of invoking the captured `onSkip` callback directly like the original two tests do. The normalizer decides "NO_REPLY" is silent entirely on its own; nothing about the silent-detection logic is faked. Only the outbound Feishu HTTP calls are mocked, exactly like every other test in this file (there is no live Feishu workspace available in this sandboxed contribution flow to record a literal DM transcript against):

```ts
it("suppresses the fallback for a real NO_REPLY block reply through the full dispatch pipeline", async () => {
  const { result, options } = createDispatcherHarness({ runtime, sessionKey: "main" });
  const { dispatcher } = createReplyDispatcherWithTyping(options);

  dispatcher.sendBlockReply({ text: "NO_REPLY" });
  await expect(result.ensureNoVisibleReplyFallback("empty-complete")).resolves.toBe(false);

  expect(sendMessageFeishuMock).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
});

it("still delivers the fallback for a real genuinely-empty block reply through the full dispatch pipeline", async () => {
  // ...same setup...
  dispatcher.sendBlockReply({ text: "" });
  await expect(result.ensureNoVisibleReplyFallback("empty-complete")).resolves.toBe(true);

  expect(sendMessageFeishuMock).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
});
```
